### Mechanism of the Week: How to Read Longevity Evidence
In 2014, Deelen and colleagues published in Human Molecular Genetics a genome-wide association study of human longevity. A commentary in Cell Cycle that year called it the largest such study to that date, and then pointed at a mismatch: genes known to extend lifespan considerably in rodents were not consistently associated with human longevity, in that scan or in genetic association studies more generally.

DNA methylation measured in 553 healthy breast-tissue samples produced a tissue-specific clock, called BTEC, whose age estimates correlated with chronological age at 0.91 and missed by a mean absolute error of 3.0 years, without the dataset-specific corrections that classical clocks needed in that tissue. ### Mechanism of the Week: Inflammaging
In a 2026 genomic cohort of 153 treatment-naive patients with six cancer types, split at age 60, tumor mutational burden was higher in the older group: a median of 4.55 mutations per megabase against 2.84.
